intl.title: Winona State - International admissions (deadlines, English proficiency, fees)

tuit.title: Winona State - International student tuition and fees

test_policy.notes: ACT and SAT are not required for admission. First-year applicants with a cumulative high school GPA of 3.0 or higher (4.0 scale) are guaranteed admission once the required courses (4 English, 3 math, 3 science, 3 social studies, 1 elective) are done; others are reviewed individually. Scores help with course placement and some scholarships. For international applicants, ACT 19 or SAT 1060 is also accepted as proof of English.

requirements.notes: International applicants pay a $20 application fee plus a $100 processing fee before review starts. Records are uploaded to the My Warrior Life portal; unofficial transcripts are enough for the decision but original or certified copies with English translation are due before the first semester. Decisions are given 2-3 weeks after all documents (first-year page). The first-year page waives the application fee for applications completed Oct 1-31, but the international page does not mention that. Some degree programs have extra entrance requirements.

english_policy.waiver_notes: The page says the English requirement may be waived in some cases; applicants log into the My Warrior Life portal to ask. ACT 19 or SAT 1060 is accepted in place of an English test. Pre-licensure Nursing needs TOEFL iBT 84 with a speaking score of 26, or IELTS 6.5 with 6.0 on every module. No conditional admission or ESL pathway is mentioned on the page.

The undergraduate cell on the page reads just '5' (graduate 110+, nursing graduate 115+), which looks like a typo, so no minimum is stored. Confirm with admissions before testing.

aid.notes: Every international student automatically receives the Cross-Cultural Scholarship, which covers the difference between resident and non-resident tuition, so they pay the Minnesota resident rate. To keep it, a student completes one cultural sharing and one cultural learning project each fall and spring semester, attends orientation and completes course OR100. No other international merit scholarship amounts are published on these pages. International students are not eligible for federal aid.
